title: device.property.reported v1
description: Emitted when a device reports property values through any ingestion protocol (MQTT, HTTP, CoAP). The event carries the reported property values and the protocol context. This schema validates only the payload; the full event must also satisfy envelope.schema.json.

tenant_id.description: Tenant boundary identifier mirrored from the envelope. Carried in the payload so consumers can validate without reaching into envelope metadata.

product_id.description: Stable internal product UUID resolved at the ingestion boundary. Used to look up the product's current thing model without an extra slug-to-id query.

device_id.description: Stable internal device UUID resolved at the ingestion boundary. Pairs with product_id for downstream tenant-scoped lookups.

tenant_slug.description: Platform-facing tenant slug used at protocol boundaries. Producers should set this from the MQTT topic segment; consumers can map it to the envelope tenant_id when needed.

device_slug.description: Platform-facing device slug within the tenant scope. Combined with tenant_id, uniquely identifies a device at protocol boundaries.

product_key.description: Identifier of the product (device model). Used to look up the thing model and validate property names.

protocol.description: Ingestion protocol used by the device. Known values include mqtt, http, coap, and websocket, but this field is intentionally open for future adapters such as modbus, opcua, or lora.

properties.description: Map of property name to value. Property names should match the product's thing model. Values can be number, boolean, or string depending on the property type.

raw.description: Optional metadata captured by the ingestion layer, such as the original source, raw payload size, or protocol-specific headers. Consumers should not depend on specific fields here.
